title: I built 30 startups in 20 years: the mistakes John Rush regrets most
summary: John Rush lists regrets from 30 startups: raising VC and hiring too early, skipping SEO, content and social, building consumer apps, free tiers in B2B, and coding from scratch. His pattern: stay lean, work with doers, validate, and market early.

principles.text: Do most of the work yourself until PMF; hiring too early hurts startups.
principles.quote: Founders should do most of the work until PMF.

principles.text: Raising VC money too early killed most of his funded startups.
principles.quote: Eventually, most of these startups failed by being funded too early.

principles.text: Start SEO early; postponing it forever is a mistake.
principles.quote: None of the people in my network did SEO. We all thought it was something too late, and we kept postponing it forever.

principles.text: Don't assume what the audience wants; validate ideas, because assumptions almost never hold.
principles.quote: I’d always assume for the audience. Anticipate what they need. It almost never turned out to be true.

principles.text: Hire doers, not managers or specialists; one fullstack dev can outpace a big team.
principles.quote: Today I have 1 fullstack dev doing 5x more progress on a project than a team of 12 back then.

principles.text: Don't start B2B with a free tier; if nobody pays, fix the product or find another audience.
principles.quote: If nobody wants to pay for my product, I have to fix it or find another audience for it.
